value.string_value: Large language models are transformer-based neural networks. They predict the next token in a sequence by computing self-attention over previous tokens. Training data quality matters more than raw model size — domain-specific fine-tuning yields disproportionate gains. The self-attention mechanism enables the model to weigh tokens across long contexts without recurrence. Diminishing returns past 70B parameters suggest that scaling alone is not sufficient. Mixture-of-experts architectures route tokens to specialized sub-networks for compute efficiency. Inference cost grows with sequence length; KV cache reuse keeps latency bounded.
